data.title: S&P 500 turns positive, but the Nasdaq indices remain in technical triage
data.description:
The broader U.S. stock indices opened lower and are trying to find their footing after the sharp declines seen recently. The S&P 500 has been the first of the three to move back into modest positive territory. The Nasdaq Composite and Nasdaq 100 have bounced off their lows but are still down on the day.

There is a difference between bouncing off a low and taking back control. For the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite, the first job is to get back above the support areas that gave way. For the Nasdaq 100, the immediate question is whether buyers can hold the retracement level tested at today’s low.

data.title: Bitcoin tests key swing area low. A break below will target the 2026 lows
data.description:
Bitcoin moved to its lowest level since early July, trading down to $61,160. That took the price $23 below the $61,183 level that marks the bottom of a key swing area on the four-hour chart, but momentum faded and the price has bounced modestly.  The buyers are trying to hold onto some control. .

The move lower extends the decline from the November 4 swing high to about $20,000, or 24.6%. From the September 21 high at $87,374, the price is down 30%. The sellers have been in control, and they are now getting another chance to push the price through support that has held since early July.

data.title: Morning Kickstart. Anthropic slides after its IPO and gold breaks lower
data.description:
Anthropic (ANT) is giving back much of its first-day gain. The stock was trading at $87.72 at 7:43 AM ET, down $9.45, or 9.7%, from Thursday’s $97.17 close. The IPO was priced at $83, and the stock traded as high as $115.10 in its debut. That leaves it just $4.72 above the offering price this morning. For me, $83 is the next barometer. A break below would erase the remaining premium to the IPO price. InvestingLive’s coverage of the Anthropic IPO pricing anthropic.com

Nasdaq 100 futures are leading the decline, European stocks are broadly lower, and Treasury yields are down across the curve. The yen and Swiss franc are the strongest of the major currencies, while gold is down about $55 despite the drop in yields and the softer dollar. On the gold chart, the break below $3,610.01 puts sellers in control heading into the North American session.

data.title: The stock market's wealth effect: why it matters even if you don't own stocks
data.description:
Equity market movements can have a significant impact on the economy through the so-called "wealth effect", changes in financial conditions and the influence on corporate investment and hiring decisions.

People can be affected by a stock market rally or selloff, even if they don't own stocks. Companies rely on financial markets to raise capital, finance expansions, make acquisitions and attract investment. When equity markets rise or collapse, the consequences can eventually reach workers, consumers and businesses across the economy.

data.title: Oil prices remain under pressure as focus shifts from supply disruptions to demand concerns. What's next?
data.description:
Crude oil has been under heavy selling pressure despite no changes on the geopolitical front. Growth concerns are likely the culprit for the weakness as lower future demand expectations naturally push prices lower despite continued supply constraints.

US-Iran tensions remain elevated despite mixed signals about renewed military action. Trump reportedly told Axios that he is in no rush to make a decision on Iran. He also indicated that any potential attack would be coordinated with Israel, which could target Iranian nuclear facilities, infrastructure and senior officials.

data.title: Gold's panic selling signals capitulation, but a catalyst is needed for a bottom
data.description:
Gold extended the selloff further despite no changes in the fundamentals. In fact, the US dollar remained relatively flat, real yields fell a bit and rate hike expectations actually eased following another rout in the stock market.

This mix would generally support gold, but it looks like we got another liquidation caused by stock market losses.
